lessons.title: Taiwan, Korea, and Singapore: Where India Fits in Asia

children.text: In 2025, South Korea's KOSPI rose 75.6% and Taiwan's TAIEX gained 25.73%, its third straight year of gains above 20%. The Nifty 50 managed about 10.5%. In May 2026, Taiwan's stock market overtook India's in total value, and Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix became a trillion-dollar company. Meanwhile, tiny Singapore sent more foreign direct investment into India in FY26 than any other country. Three places with a combined population smaller than Uttar Pradesh have enormous influence over where Asian money goes, and over how Indian stocks perform relative to their neighbours.

body.text: Taiwan and Korea are the stock markets of the global AI hardware supply chain. Singapore is Asia's financial hub and India's biggest investment conduit. India's market is built on domestic consumption, financials and services, which is exactly why it often zigs when they zag.

children.text: Taiwan: One Company, One Island, One Global Bottleneck

markDefs.definition: A company that manufactures chips designed by other companies. TSMC is the world's leading foundry, making advanced chips for firms such as Nvidia and Apple.

children.text: Taiwan's market is dominated by a single company: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, or TSMC, the world's leading chip

. Almost every advanced AI chip, from Nvidia's processors to Apple's, is made in its factories. TSMC alone made up about 42% of the TAIEX in May 2026, and its market value was roughly $2 trillion in September 2026. Around it sits a cluster of chip designers, server makers and component suppliers. When global AI spending booms, Taiwan booms. When the AI trade wobbles, Taiwan's market can drop like a stone.

cells: Taiwan Stock Exchange (TWSE), plus the Taipei Exchange (TPEx) for smaller companies
TAIEX, a market cap-weighted index of TWSE-listed shares
TSMC, about 42% of the TAIEX in May 2026
Overtook India in May 2026 at about $4.95 trillion, before India regained fifth place in late June
Emerging market, and the largest country in the MSCI EM Index in 2026
Concentration in chips and TSMC, the AI spending cycle, and geopolitical tension with China

body.title: Taiwan's AI rally
body.prompt: The TAIEX closed 2025 at 28,963.60. On 1 August 2026, after a record one-day jump, it closed at 43,119.75. What was its percentage gain over that period? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: Gain = (43,119.75 ÷ 28,963.60 − 1) × 100 = (1.4888 − 1) × 100 = 48.9% in seven months. The same day's 7.98% jump came right after one of the biggest falls in the index's history in late July. Markets concentrated in one theme can deliver huge gains, but with violent swings in both directions.

body.text: Taiwan is a concentrated bet on two things: the AI chip cycle and geopolitical stability. With TSMC at around 42% of the index, a problem at one company or a rise in tension across the Taiwan Strait can hit the entire market. India's Nifty 50 is concentrated too, but in banks, not in a single company or technology.

children.text: South Korea: Chaebol, Chips and the Korea Discount

markDefs.definition: A large family-controlled Korean business group, such as Samsung, SK, Hyundai or LG, often spread across many listed companies connected by cross-holdings. Similar in structure to India's large promoter-led business houses.

The long-standing tendency of Korean stocks to trade at lower valuations than similar companies elsewhere, blamed on weak governance, low shareholder payouts and the interests of controlling families.

children.text: Korea's stock market is run by Korea Exchange (KRX). Its main index is the KOSPI, and the tech-heavy KOSDAQ covers smaller growth companies. Two memory chip giants, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, dominate the index, with market values of roughly $1.23 trillion and $894 billion in September 2026. Much of Korean business is organised into
, family-run groups whose decisions have not always favoured minority shareholders. That created the

. Inspired by Japan, Korea launched a Corporate Value-Up Program in 2024. In 2025 it amended its Commercial Act to make directors owe a duty to all shareholders, not just the company, and in 2026 it tackled the use of treasury shares by controlling families.

body.title: Measure Korea's pullback
body.prompt: The KOSPI closed at 8,476.15 on 29 May 2026 and at 6,909.91 on 11 September 2026. What was the percentage fall? Enter a negative number, rounded to one decimal place.
body.explanation: Change = (6,909.91 ÷ 8,476.15 − 1) × 100 = (0.8152 − 1) × 100 = −18.5%. A fall of that size in about three and a half months would be a major correction for the Nifty. For a market that rose 75.6% in one year and kept surging into 2026, it is part of the ride. High returns and high volatility travel together.

body.title: Why was Korea cheap for so long?
body.question: Which of these best explains the historical "Korea discount"?
options: Korea was not a member of any MSCI index
Weak governance at family-controlled groups, low payouts to shareholders and decisions that favoured controlling families
Korean shares could only be bought by domestic investors
body.explanation: Korean companies such as Samsung have long been highly profitable and globally competitive. The discount came from governance: controlling families could make decisions that benefited themselves at the expense of minority shareholders, and companies often hoarded cash rather than paying dividends or buying back shares. Korea's Value-Up Program and Commercial Act changes target exactly these issues. Indian investors will recognise similar debates around promoter-controlled companies.

children.text: Singapore: Asia's Financial Hub and India's Gateway

Singapore's stock market is small, but its role as a financial centre is huge. Singapore Exchange (SGX) runs the Straits Times Index (STI) of 30 leading companies, and its three big banks, DBS, OCBC and UOB, made up about 54% of the index by 2024. That makes the STI a steady, dividend-rich market that reacts to interest rates more than to technology cycles. It hit a record above 5,000 in February 2026. To attract more investors, Singapore launched a S$5 billion Equity Market Development Programme in 2025, expanded to S$6.5 billion in 2026, and announced a dual listing bridge with Nasdaq.

For Indian investors, Singapore matters mainly as a source of money. It is India's largest source of foreign direct investment, with about $194.7 billion of equity inflows since April 2000. Its sovereign investors, GIC and Temasek, are among the largest foreign shareholders in Indian companies, and many global funds invest in India through Singapore-based entities. Until July 2023, the Nifty's overnight futures traded in Singapore as SGX Nifty, before moving to GIFT City as GIFT Nifty.

body.title: Singapore's share of India's FDI
body.prompt: India received FDI equity inflows of $58.85 billion in FY26, of which $19.8 billion came from Singapore. What share of India's FDI came from Singapore, in percent? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: Share = $19.8 billion ÷ $58.85 billion × 100 = 33.6%. About one in every three dollars of FDI into India came through Singapore, far ahead of Mauritius at $6.57 billion and Japan at $3.74 billion. Part of this reflects Singapore's role as a regional base for global companies and funds, not just Singaporean money.

body.title: Korea's early start
body.textWithBlank: Korea is 3 hours 30 minutes ahead of India, so the KOSPI opens at 9:00 am Korea time, which is ___ IST.
body.explanation: 9:00 am minus 3 hours 30 minutes is 5:30 am IST, the same time Tokyo opens. Korea and Japan give Indian investors the earliest read on how Asia is absorbing overnight US news, especially for technology and chip stocks.

body.caption: How India compares with its Asian neighbours

cells: Banks and financials, IT services, energy, consumer
Value-Up reforms against the Korea discount

body.text: India's missing piece is listed AI hardware. It has no TSMC, Samsung or SK Hynix. So when global investors chase the AI boom, money flows to Taiwan and Korea, and India's share of emerging market funds shrinks, as it did from nearly 21% of the MSCI EM Index in 2024 to about 12% in 2026. When the AI trade cools, India's domestic growth story and its lower dependence on chips can make it look attractive again. India is building towards this through its semiconductor mission, including Tata Electronics' fab at Dholera with Taiwan's PSMC and Micron's assembly and test plant at Sanand.

body.title: An AI blowout overnight
body.scenario: Overnight, a leading US AI chip company reports results far above expectations and raises its forecast. At 5:30 am IST, the KOSPI opens 3.5% higher, and at 6:30 am the TAIEX opens up 4%. GIFT Nifty is up only 0.3%. You hold a Nifty 50 index fund, HDFC Bank, Infosys and an Indian electronics manufacturing company.
body.prompt: Explain why Korea and Taiwan are reacting so much more strongly than India, how each of your holdings might be affected, and what this could mean for foreign flows into India over the next few weeks.
body.modelAnswer:
Why the difference:
1. Taiwan and Korea are directly in the AI chip supply chain. TSMC manufactures the US company's chips, and SK Hynix and Samsung supply high-performance memory. Better AI demand means higher expected profits for them.
2. India has no large listed chipmakers, so the direct earnings impact on the Nifty is small. GIFT Nifty's small gain reflects mostly positive global mood.

Your holdings:
1. Nifty 50 fund: A mild positive open driven by sentiment, not earnings.
2. HDFC Bank: Little direct link. It will move with broader Indian factors.
3. Infosys: Could benefit modestly if stronger AI spending supports demand for IT and AI services, though the link is indirect.
4. Electronics manufacturer: May see some positive sentiment as a supply chain player, but it assembles and manufactures rather than making advanced chips.

Foreign flows: If the AI rally continues, emerging market funds may add to Taiwan and Korea and trim India, as happened when India's MSCI EM weight shrank in 2025 and 2026. Watch NSDL FPI data and relative performance over several weeks rather than reacting to one morning.

body.title: Track Asia's other big three
steps: At 5:30 am IST, check the KOSPI open along with the Nikkei, and note Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
At 6:30 am IST, check the TAIEX and TSMC's move for a read on the AI chip trade.
Check the Straits Times Index and Singapore banks for regional interest rate and risk sentiment.
Compare Asian moves with GIFT Nifty to see whether India is following the region or its own story.
Each month, compare India's MSCI EM weight and FPI flows with Taiwan and Korea to spot rotation.

points: Taiwan's market is a concentrated bet on AI chips: TSMC was about 42% of the TAIEX in May 2026, and the index gained 25.73% in 2025 and nearly 49% more by August 2026.
Korea's KOSPI rose 75.6% in 2025 on memory chip demand and Value-Up governance reforms aimed at the Korea discount, but fell 18.5% from late May to mid-September 2026.
Singapore's STI is dominated by three banks and trades on interest rates, while Singapore itself supplied $19.8 billion, or about a third, of India's FDI in FY26.
Korea opens at 5:30 am IST, Taiwan at 6:30 am and Singapore at 6:30 am, so all three give early signals before NSE opens.
India's market is driven by domestic growth, financials and services, and it lacks listed AI hardware champions. That is why it lagged Taiwan and Korea during the AI rally.
When AI enthusiasm runs hot, foreign money tends to rotate towards Taiwan and Korea and away from India. When it cools, India's domestic story can regain favour.
